edition.note: Open Library record for ISBN 9780062560704: Harper Business, 2017, edition_name "First edition." Apple Books lists release July 18, 2017 (https://books.apple.com/se/book/angel/id1166101041). No revised edition found; the author's 2023 "Angel Investor" is listed as a separate book. Chapter numbers were not checked against a table of contents.

rows.claim: Because you cannot know in advance which company will be the outlier, Calacanis says to spread small checks across at least 30 startups.
rows.note: Secondary source: reader notes that reproduce book passages show "you are going to need to invest in fifty startups (diversification!) in Silicon Valley (location!) over three years" and "$1.5 million to work in these fifty deals". Two more secondary pages agree on 50 over three years (https://jdlasica.com/?p=9357, https://www.maxmednik.com/blog/notes-on-angel-by-jason-calacanis). "At least 30" was not found; the only 30 is "first 30 angel investments" on product/market fit. Card changed to fifty startups over three years; "small checks" dropped (book average is $30,000 per deal). Passage not seen in the book itself.

rows.claim: Applied: with about €40k, the 30-startup spread does not fit, so in your roadmap angel bets could at most live in the 20 percent satellite.
rows.note: The "30-startup spread" repeated the unconfirmed figure from p5; now "fifty-startup spread", per the same passage. The €40k and the 20 percent satellite are the reader's own roadmap figures, not book claims.

rows.claim: Your 80 percent index core is built on the opposite logic: own the whole market and accept its average, instead of hunting the outlier.
rows.note: The Card attributes no figure or quote to the book: the 80 percent index core is the reader's own roadmap. The contrast it draws (hunting the outlier) matches the book as noted: fifty deals "in order to have a chance at an outsize return". Card unchanged.

rows.claim: Check on p5: "Across how many startups does Calacanis say to spread checks?" Correct option "At least 30 startups".
rows.note: Prompt, fare and options changed to match the corrected p5: correct option now "Fifty startups over three years"; second option reworded to keep option lengths close.
